subject: Pilot affordability & batching levers — recap and next steps
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot affordability & batching levers — recap and next steps

Hi Maya / Alex —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick written recap so we have a single view and clear next steps. I pulled together the assumptions we discussed and called out where we think Redwood can make measurable TCO impact in an initial pilot.

Summary of customer pain and goals
- Primary pain: inference spend is growing unpredictably as usage scales (esp. embedding + chat routes). Budget gate in Q3 — need a bounded pilot that demonstrates per-session cost reduction.
- Secondary: occasional latency spikes during peak auth flows; reliability requirements for fraud detections.
- Goal: prove a 30–50% unit-cost reduction on a narrow user path within 8 weeks and surface operational runbooks for productionizing batching/caching.

Key levers we discussed (how Redwood helps)
- Continuous batching: group short requests from the fraud-check route to improve GPU utilization with sub-50ms added queuing for this path. Expected token-cost reduction: 15–30% depending on concurrency.
- Prefix/KV caching: for repeated prompt prefixes (user metadata + policy text) we can cache KV state and reduce repeated compute on ACU-heavy tokens. Expected savings: 10–25% on repeated flows.
- Model variant routing: fall back to a cheaper quantized variant for non-critical assistant responses and reserve higher-FP variant for high-confidence fraud flags. Savings: 5–15% depending on split.

Assumptions (please confirm)
- Current 30-day avg for the target route: ~2.4M tokens/day (flux-usage-snapshot.csv attached).
- Target pilot scope: 20% of production traffic (production-like surface).
- SLA tolerance for pilot: up to 100ms p50 increase on the instrumented route for batching tradeoffs.

Proposed pilot next steps & timeline
1) Redwood to send pilot SOW + pricing model by EOD Wed (we will include three budget scenarios and expected ROI at 4 and 8 weeks).
2) Flux to confirm target route(s) and any security packaging needs (VPC, logging retention) by Fri 6/18.
3) Kickoff & baseline measurement window (1 week) then 8-week pilot with checkpoints at week 2 and week 6.

Deliverables we will provide
- Pilot SOW (SLA, instrumentation checklist, rollback plan)
- Pricing model workbook with sensitivity on concurrency, batching delay, and model split (attached: redwood-pilot-pricing-model.xlsx)
- Ops checklist for caching rules + suggested prompts to prioritize for prefix caching

Ask from you now
- Confirm the target route names (exact path or API route) and whether you want us to include embedding-heavy routes in scope.
- Share any hard budget caps that should constrain our pricing scenarios.

Attachments: flux-usage-snapshot.csv (usage export), redwood-pilot-pricing-model.xlsx (draft), pilot-scope-onepager.pdf

Thanks — will follow up with the SOW this afternoon.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-pilot-pricing-model.xlsx (xlsx, 56 KB)]

Hi Grace —

Thanks for the clear summary — very helpful. Quick answers:
- Confirmed route: /api/v1/fraud/check (this is the high-volume path).
- We'll exclude embedding-heavy analytics routes from the initial scope; focus on fraud/check and the user-notify assistant replies.
- Budget: our procurement gate expects the pilot to demonstrate >=30% unit-cost reduction or else we won't expand. We can commit up to $60k for the pilot if the SOW shows projected savings that meet that threshold.

Two asks for your SOW/pricing workbook:
1) Can you show a sensitivity column that assumes 25%, 40%, and 60% of traffic opt-in to batching (we have spikes tied to peak business hours).
2) We need an estimate on how prefix caching might affect false-positive rates for the fraud route (if at all). If that requires more technical detail, happy to loop in our infra lead.

I can do a quick sync Thurs 6/17 at 10am PT to walk the workbook — does that work for you?

— Maya
Head of Product | Flux Financial

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot affordability & batching levers — technical notes

Grace / Marissa —

Notes from an engineering perspective to include in the SOW/pricing workbook:
- Batching config: target 40–60ms batching window on /api/v1/fraud/check during off-peak to maximize payloads; reduce to 15–20ms during peak hours with dynamic policy to avoid customer-visible latency. This yields an expected 18–28% token cost reduction on the route in our sims (see attached quick sim in Drive link).
- KV caching: safe for deterministic prefix material (policy text, app prompts). For anything that includes per-request ephemeral signals (session-specific nonces, timestamps) we should avoid caching those tokens. Impact to model correctness should be negligible if we layer caching at the tokenizer/KV level and invalidate on session resets. We'll add a short test plan for false-positive monitoring (fconf checks) — expectation: <0.5% drift in fraud flag rate with conservative cache TTLs.
- Rollback: automatic model-variant fallback if p95 latency exceeds configured threshold or if drift > 1% on fraud-detection precision.

I'll add these to the SOW doc and the pricing sheet — will include the sim output and a conservative ROI table for the 30/50% savings buckets.

-Jonas
Staff Engineer, Inference Runtime | Redwood Inference
